parsed.summary: The first theorem proves a universal c > 0 such that, for every finite game with nonempty answer sets and ε = 1 − ω*(G) > 0, every n ≥ 1 satisfies ω*(G^{⊗n}) < exp(−c·ε¹³/(ε + log(|A||B|))·n). The second proves that every finite game with ω*(G) < 1 satisfies ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ C·e^{−cn} for some c, C > 0. Here ω* is the supremum over finite-dimensional tensor-product strategies with mixed states and POVMs. The main caveat is that the second theorem allows a prefactor C, whereas the paper's conjecture has no prefactor. The two forms are equivalent using ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ ω*(G) < 1, and the first theorem implies the paper form anyway, so this is low severity.

glossary.plain: Finite game: a probability distribution µ on X×Y and a Boolean predicate V(x,y,a,b).
G^{⊗n}: the product distribution µ^n, winning iff every coordinate wins.
PSD effects summing to the identity
Finite-dimensional spaces H_A, H_B (in Type 0), a state ρ on H_A⊗H_B, and POVMs indexed by questions.
glossary.note: Finite-dimensional only; this is the standard ω* model. The paper's precise model is not in the excerpt.

glossary.plain: Supremum of the win probability over all strategies
glossary.note: The set is bounded by 1. It is nonempty when A and B are nonempty. If A is empty it gives the junk value 0, but that case is excluded or harmless.

glossary.plain: There exist c, C > 0 with v n ≤ C e^{−cn} for all n
glossary.note: Has a prefactor C. Equivalent to the paper's form given monotonicity of ω*(G^{⊗n}) in n.

lean_claims.plain: There exists c > 0 such that for all finite X, Y, A, B (Type 0), every game G with A and B nonempty, and ε := 1 − ω*(G) > 0, and every n ≥ 1: ω*(G^n) < exp(−c·ε¹³/(ε + ln(|A||B|))·n).
For every finite game G with ω*(G) < 1, there exist c, C > 0 with ω*(G^n) ≤ C e^{−cn} for all n ∈ ℕ.

paper_claims.plain: There is a universal c_qs > 0 such that for every finite game with nonempty answer alphabets and ε = 1 − ω*(G) > 0, ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ exp(−c_qs ε¹³/(ε + log|A||B|)·n) for all n ≥ 1.
For every finite game with ω*(G) < 1, there exists c_G > 0 with ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ exp(−c_G n) for all n ≥ 1.

coverage.why: Strict inequality instead of ≤. Otherwise identical; the log base is absorbed into c.
The prefactor C can be removed using ω*(G^n) ≤ ω*(G) < 1.

flags.explanation: A prefactor C > 0 is allowed, while the paper uses exp(−c_G n) with no prefactor. This is formally weaker. It is mathematically equivalent via monotonicity of the repeated value, and Theorem 1.1's formalization already gives the C = 1 form.
flags.probe_idea: Derive ∃ c>0, ∀ n≥1, repeatedEntangledValue G n ≤ exp(-c n) from distributionUniformExponential.

flags.explanation: Strict < is used where the paper states ≤.
Strategies are restricted to finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces in Type 0, i.e., the tensor-product ω*. The paper's precise model is not in the excerpt; commuting-operator values would differ.
